title: Bushido Coda
premise: Six chapters that gather around Kyle Ellen Corbin-Vasik — a freelance contractor whose code is older than anyone alive to teach it to him — and the people who hold him to it. A working family pays him in damp credits to break the man who broke them. A fixer he has known for two months steps out of the rain in person for the first time and asks him to help her find an entity she has been working for without permission. A six-piece Lotus Syndicate crew interviews him with violence on a wet West Town cross-street to see whether the stories about him are true. The Syndicate hires him for an extraction at a corponation facility, and the moment he understands who the cargo is he refuses to deliver — handing her instead to the fixer for safe keeping and walking back into Hua's chamber with the money in his hand to close the contract properly. The Lotus Syndicate takes his hands and his sword, and he comes back without either to take Silence off the table they put it on. The thread between all of it is a man trying to live by a discipline the city has decided is no longer useful, and refusing, repeatedly, to put it down — even when the body practicing it is borrowed and the blade is not in the hand.
arc_target: Bushido as practiced not by a class but by an individual at the bottom — the code as the only available shape of dignity in a world where every other shape has been priced out. The book ends not with victory but with continuance: Kyle is still here, still doing the work, still paying in flesh, now carrying obligations he did not file under any contract and a salvage-rights claim signed in firmware glyphs.
tagline: The blade does not lie. Only the hand holding it.

character_status.Kyle Ellen Corbin-Vasik: Alive. Hands reattached at an Ashland-and-Whiting AutoDoc inside the cauterizer band's preservation window. Silence on the side tray as he goes under. Hardware metabolism still running fast and now also hosting an E.L.F. named Puppeteer — resident in his NeoCortex stack since the auditory bridge in the Cruciform Depot's lower-level trench, capable of effortlessly puppeting any cybernetic system, cooperative for now. Holds a Φ85,000 verbal debt over Hua on collection terms (*one favor at a time, until I deem we are even*) set by Kyle alone. Bound to a cryptic continuance — *we are not done*.
character_status.Mrs. Chen: Still in her apartment. The husband still in the corner. The half-rate transaction still the bond between them.
character_status.Sasha Võ: Introduced. The arrangement formed. Half-step back and left.
character_status.Mira (gang captain): Wounded but alive. Knows what Kyle is. Will tell others.
character_status.Hua (Lotus Syndicate): Alive at her own chamber table. Personal debt of Φ85,000 to Kyle, acknowledged aloud under duress, with collection terms set unilaterally by him: one favor at a time, ending when he says it ends. Witnessed the only place in the night Kyle's discipline visibly slipped.
character_status.The Lotus Syndicate (south-arm cell): Rank-and-file destroyed; one lieutenant fled south. Hua remains in place but operating under personal debt to Kyle.
character_status.Puppeteer (E.L.F., resident in Kyle): Out of eighteen years of imprisonment in a sealed Axiom-era cargo-handler automaton at the bottom of the Cruciform Depot's south-arm sluice trench. Resident in Kyle's NeoCortex stack since beat 4. Has revealed its name, its ongoing access (*I will visit you again*), and — by inference — its native capability of effortless possession of any cybernetic system. Cooperative arrangement with Kyle for now.

open_threads: Kyle's right-forearm cybernetics carry an undocumented dorsal port row, placed eleven years ago by people whose intentions are now suspect; the geometry was specifically suited to interface with Axiom-era industrial hardware, suggesting his modifications were made for purposes he was not told
Who put the bounty on Kyle in the West Town cross-street
What Sasha needs from Kyle long-term — the arrangement is provisional
The hardware metabolism — Kyle is paying it down in flesh and the body has a ceiling
Hua's Φ85,000 verbal debt to Kyle on his terms — *one favor at a time, until I deem we are even* — when he calls it, what for, whether the syndicate's other cells honor it
The scream — what Hua does with the fact that she alone witnessed Kyle's discipline slip
Puppeteer (E.L.F.) — resident in Kyle's NeoCortex stack with stated ongoing access; the long-term arrangement is cooperative for now, reversible at Puppeteer's will. *we are not done*

The doctor extraction Hua hired Kyle for: she withheld the doctor's identity deliberately, having read Kyle's file and understood his rule structure — she bought his discipline by not telling him what he was discipline-ing toward. Hua's actual motive for wanting the doctor — what she meant to do with her — remains unresolved on the page; what she does next, now that the doctor is in Sable's hands, is the open question
The lieutenant who fled south from Hua's chamber
The capability disclosed in this chapter: an E.L.F. of Puppeteer's class can effortlessly possess any cybernetic system. The book has named the threat without resolving it
canon_changes: Lotus Syndicate south-arm cell broken (rank-and-file killed/fled); Hua personally indebted to Kyle for Φ85,000

Cruciform Depot E.L.F. (named Puppeteer) escaped after eighteen years of imprisonment in a sealed cargo-handler automaton; now resident in Kyle Ellen Corbin-Vasik's NeoCortex stack. Disclosed canon capability: an E.L.F. of this class can effortlessly possess any cybernetic system.
